sources.quote: Harriot's small treatise on the collision of round bodies, the De reflexione corporum rotundorum was prepared in 1619 for his patron Henry Percy, ninth Earl of Northumberland
We know from a letter accompanying this treatise, that Harriot shared his ideas with both Warner, and another friend and member of the Percy household, Robert Hues
he had privileged access to some of it even before it was published, via his friend Torporley, who had acted as Viète's amanuensis in the mid-1590s.
Both of these publications showed Harriot's initial debt to the algebraic work of the French mathematician François Viète, but also the extent of his own original contributions.

note: Stedall reconstructed and published Harriot's manuscripts.

sources.quote: Stedall was able to reconstruct this unpublished treatise on equations from 140 scattered sheets in the surviving manuscripts.

note: Schemmel analyzed Harriot's work on mechanics.

sources.quote: Schemmel's close analysis of Harriot's research methods reveal a figure in whose work 'we […can] discern several of the crucial insights for which Galileo was famous'.

note: Harriot's manuscripts are held at the British Library.

sources.quote: the De numeris triangularibus. et inde de progressionibus arithmeticis magisteria magna, which survives in British Library, Additional MS 6782.
